author: Lone Star Standard
title: Texas Apartment Association supports Entryway initiative aiding rental housing workforce
text:
The Texas Apartment Association (TAA) has announced its support for Entryway, a nonprofit organization focused on helping individuals facing housing insecurity gain employment and stable housing within the rental housing industry. Entryway provides skill-building, job placement, and access to stable housing for people seeking long-term self-sufficiency.
According to TAA, Entryway’s approach is rooted in “Dignity, Accountability, and Opportunity,” which guide how they work with program participants and industry partners. The organization prepares individuals for roles in property management, maintenance, leasing, and other key positions that are essential to the rental housing sector.
“Entryway offers more than a handout, they provide real change. Through skill-building, full-time job placement, and access to stable housing, they empower individuals to step into long-term self-sufficiency. Their approach aligns with our values at TAA: creating opportunity, building community, and delivering measurable, meaningful impact,” the association stated.
TAA President Renee Zahn of Greystar selected Entryway as the association’s 2025 charitable initiative. The Texas Suppliers Council chaired by Jackie Cagle of Rasa Floors has helped raise over $12,800 from more than 100 donors so far. TAA aims to reach a fundraising goal of $50,000 by year-end; all funds will support training programs, housing assistance, and employment opportunities for those overcoming homelessness.
“What sets Entryway apart is their unwavering dedication to Dignity, Accountability, and Opportunity. These guiding principles inform how they serve program participants, engage with industry partners, and foster a respectful, empowering culture within their organization. As they expand, these core values remain constant to ensure every person is treated with respect and equipped for success,” TAA added.
Entryway collaborates with nonprofits, employers, volunteers, and sponsors across Texas to build a talent pipeline while addressing workforce gaps in the rental housing sector.
“Their work isn’t just life-changing for individuals—it benefits our industry as well. By preparing motivated individuals for careers in property management, maintenance, leasing and other vital roles—Entryway is helping fill workforce gaps while transforming lives across Texas and beyond. Their collaborative model brings together nonprofits employers volunteers and sponsors to create meaningful lasting partnerships plus a pipeline of talent that benefits everyone involved,” said TAA.
“We’re excited to share that Entryway has been selected as TAA’s 2025 charitable initiative by TAA President Renee Zahn with Greystar—and we look forward to supporting this important mission throughout the year. Thanks to the generosity of the TAA community and the leadership of the Texas Suppliers Council chaired by Jackie Cagle with Rasa Floors we’ve already raised more than $12 800 from over 100 donors But we’re just getting started! Our goal is to raise $50 000 by the end of the year—and every dollar goes directly toward supporting training housing and employment for those working to overcome homelessness and achieve stability.”
The association encourages further donations through https://give.entrywaytalent.org/campaign/659178/donate.
